We report the first detection of hot molecular cores in a supernova remnant using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array.
The detected hot cores (HC1 and HC2) are located inside the X-ray shell of the young supernova remnant RX J1713.7$-$3946, and both sources are associated with Class I intermediate-mass protostars.

Despite being located within a supernova-feedback region, the column density ratios of complex organic molecules (HCOOCH$_3$/CH$_3$OH, CH$_3$OCH$_3$/CH$_3$OH, and CH$_3$CHO/CH$_3$OH), a deuterated molecule (CH$_2$DOH/CH$_3$OH), and sulfur- and nitrogen-bearing species (OCS/CH$_3$OH and C$_2$H$_5$CN/CH$_3$CN) in HC1 are indistinguishable from those observed in hot cores/corinos in more typical star-forming environments.
